//: SwayNotificationCenter. Replaces mako, which had no config anywhere on this
system and therefore ran at its compiled defaults: a #285577 blue box with a
#4C7899 border that never expired (default-timeout=0). That was the last
surface on this desktop still showing stock colours.
It is here rather than a mako config for three reasons: the control centre
gives the volume slider, the media player and the quick toggles a real CSS
panel; it renders the `int:value` hint as a progress bar, which turns the
UNTOUCHED /usr/share/sway/config.d/60-bindings-{volume,brightness}.conf into
a proper OSD (those already send -h int:value:$VALUE; mako discarded it); and
it is themable from one stylesheet.
IMPORTANT: unlike waybar/rofi/swaylock/mako, this file is NOT a wholesale
replacement of the shipped /etc/xdg/swaync/config.json. swaync resolves each
key against its own COMPILED-IN defaults -- swaync(5) documents a `default:`
per option -- so an omitted key falls back to the compiled value and NOT to
whatever the shipped sample says. That file is a sample, not a base layer.
Hence every key the theme depends on is restated here even where it matches;
cssPriority in particular has a compiled default of `application` while the
sample sets `user`.
Started as a systemd user unit wanted by sway-session.target, so it owns
org.freedesktop.Notifications before anything can ask for it -- mako ships a
D-Bus activation entry claiming the same name, and which one wins is not
something to rely on. See build_files/10-sway-install.sh.
// theme: Both required for the stylesheet to take effect. ignore-gtk-theme unsets GTK_THEME so adw-gtk3-dark does not fight the CSS; cssPriority=user loads it above ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css.
// placement: Top right, under the 22px bar. layer=overlay so popups sit above fullscreen windows; control-center-layer=top so the panel does not.
// timeouts: The fix for mako's never-expiring popup. Critical stays at 0 (sticky) on purpose -- that is the one class that should wait to be read.
// geometry: Both monitors are 1920 logical wide -- the Dell is 3840 at scale 2 -- so one
320 rather than swaync's default of 500: this panel holds a switch, a
slider, a media card and a row of four buttons, none of which needs the
width, and at 500 it read as a page rather than as a flyout. 320 is about
the floor -- four toggles across it are ~70px each, and the media card
still fits a file name and five transport buttons. The popup width follows
it down, 20px narrower again so a notification never looks wider than the
The body-image box comes down with them: 180px of image in a 360px popup
left the text in a column too narrow to read.
There is no panel height any more. `fit-to-screen: true` expands the
control centre to the full height of whatever monitor it opens on, which
is also why control-center-height is left at a value it never uses:
swaync(5) says it is ignored while fit-to-screen is true, and deriving the
height from the monitor beats naming a number that is wrong on the other
one. The sections sit at the top; the notification list is `vexpand` and
takes all the slack, and since the container is transparent that slack is
// text-empty: Empty, and that is deliberate now: the container is transparent, so a placeholder would be a label and a large icon floating on the bare desktop with nothing behind them. style.css hides the placeholder outright for the same reason.
// widgets: Order is top to bottom in the panel. This is where the volume / media /
toggle UI actually comes from -- they are first-class widgets, not scripts.
dnd          do-not-disturb switch
volume       a real slider, plus per-device rows. swaync links libpulse
directly, so this needs no helper.
mpris        track name and transport. playerctl is already
installed and the media keys are already bound by Fedora's
60-bindings-media.conf; this is the missing surface.
buttons-grid quick toggles, below.
notifications the history list. vexpand so it takes the slack.
NO HARDWARE GAUGES HERE, and not for want of trying. cpu/memory/
temperature came off waybar when the bar was reduced to glyphs, and this
panel is the obvious place for them, but swaync 0.12.6 cannot display a
live number:
`label` takes a static string from this file. There is no swaync-client
verb that changes it at runtime, so the only way to refresh it would be
to rewrite this file and reload the config -- and this file is a symlink
into a git repo.
`slider` looks like the answer: cmd_getter is documented as running on
every visibility change of the control centre, which is exactly the
refresh a gauge needs. It does run -- proven with a getter that touched
a file -- but 0.12.6 never applies the result to the scale. Three
gauges fed `echo 25`, `printf 40` and `echo 100`, in ranges 0-100 and
0-1, all sat pinned at the minimum. It is a read that goes nowhere.
So the numbers went to the one surface on this desktop that can render
live text on demand: the tooltip of waybar's custom/hardware module, one
glyph in the bar's status pill, fed by waybar/stats.sh. If a later swaync
fixes the slider, three `slider#cpu`-style widgets pointed at
`sh -c '$HOME/.config/waybar/stats.sh cpu'` are all this needs -- the
script already prints exactly what a 0-100 slider wants.
// no title widget: The header is gone. It was a card that spent its whole height saying
`Notifications` -- above a panel whose only contents are notifications --
Clearing did not go with it: middle-click the bell on the bar, which
keep their own close button either way.

// mpris: Transport and track name, and nothing else. `show-album-art: never` is
the whole of it -- accepted values are always | never | when-available.
image-size and image-radius are gone with it: both only ever sized the
artwork, so with the artwork off they configure nothing.
ONE SECTION PER ACTIVE PLAYER, STACKED. The three mpris#... widgets in
the list above are the same widget three times: swaync keys widget
config on ^<name>(#[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)?$, so an instance is a real feature
rather than a trick, and three instances are three sections down the
panel instead of one.
This is the only way to get players side by side vertically. A single
mpris widget puts them in a CAROUSEL -- one visible at a time, with
arrows and page dots -- and that is built into the widget, not styling:
nothing in CSS reflows an Adw carousel into a column.
One instance per APP, narrowed with an inverted blacklist -- the
blacklist is a regex over the bus name, so `^(?!.*chromium).*$` on the
#chrome instance means everything EXCEPT Chrome. #other then takes what
is left by naming the apps the others claimed, so a player nobody
anticipated gets a section rather than vanishing.
Per app, not per player, and that is the one case this cannot split: a
bus name is org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.<app>.instance<pid>, and the pid is
not knowable in advance, so two windows of the SAME app share their
section as a two-page carousel. Two different apps always get two
sections.
The empty instances cost nothing on screen -- autohide, below, keeps
each one off the panel until its app is actually playing -- so the list
is written long deliberately. Adding an app is five lines here and one
entry in #other's blacklist.
`autohide` is what makes ACTIVE the operative word. It hides a widget
when its player has no metadata, and with one player per widget that
finally means what it says: Chrome parks a session on the bus Stopped,
with no title and no url, for as long as the browser is open, and the
#browser section stays off the panel until a tab actually plays. The
same option did nothing when every player shared one widget -- one
player with metadata kept the whole thing visible -- which is why an
empty Chrome card used to sit beside the real one.
playerctld is excluded everywhere, and by construction: it matches none
of the app patterns, so every inverted regex blacklists it, and #other
names it outright. It is a proxy that mirrors whichever player is
active, so a section for it would duplicate whichever section is already
showing. Nothing else points at it either: waybar held the desktop's
only playerctld consumer, and that mpris module is gone too now that
now-playing lives here.
THERE IS NO SEEK BAR TO KEEP. This widget's layout is a GtkBuilder
template compiled into swaync, and it holds exactly: a background
picture, a 96px album-art image, a title label, a subtitle label, and
five flat buttons -- shuffle, previous, play/pause, next, repeat. No
progress scale, no position label. (The binary does carry a `can_seek`
query, but nothing in the template draws with it.) An older comment here
credited this widget with `scrub position`; it never had one.

//: Toggles, not pickers. A `toggle` button needs BOTH command (the
action) and update-command, which prints true/false so the button
renders the system's real state rather than a remembered one -- open
the panel after changing wifi from the CLI and it should already agree.
EVERY COMMAND HERE IS A CALL INTO swaync/toggle.sh, and that is a bug
fix rather than a refactor. These used to be inline one-liners, and
swaync does not run them through a shell: it expands the string itself
and spawns an argv, which tears apart anything containing a double
quote or a $(...). Opening the panel logged
-g: -c: line 1: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `''
once for wifi and once for bluetooth, every time. Their update-commands
never ran, so both buttons showed the `active: false` default no matter
what the radios were doing -- while the idle toggle, whose one-liner
happened to contain neither a double quote nor a substitution, worked
and made the other two look like a styling problem.
`sh -c '<script> <name> <verb>'` is the shape that survives: one level
of quoting, no substitution. toggle.sh carries the reasoning for each
of the three, and the reason the fourth is not a toggle.
Glyphs are the literal Nerd Font characters, written the same way
waybar/config.jsonc writes its own -- and wifi/bluetooth are the very
same codepoints (U+F05A9, U+F00AF) so the panel and the bar cannot
drift apart. No padding: this is the *Mono* variant, which forces every
glyph to one cell, so the four buttons are already equal width. Do not
pad with U+3000 -- Hack Nerd Font Mono has no ideographic space and it
renders as a fallback box.
